RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 25

The panel's composition alone proves nothing. All-female panels occur routinely by chance and by discipline demographics, and there's no evidence they favour female candidates — research generally finds little or no such effect. Leading with it will make you look aggrieved rather than credible, and it's the weakest part of your case.

Your strong points are concrete: you pursue the written reasons you're legally or procedurally entitled to, then ask how the stated criteria were weighted — specifically how "finishing a PhD" and two papers scored against a completed PhD and six, and whether industry experience was in the advertised criteria. If the criteria were changed or applied inconsistently, that's actionable. Escalate to HR or the ombudsman on process, not panel gender.
